result.summary:
Independent gate of docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md, read in full directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Handoff explicitly flagged this as the 5th consecutive gate at risk of the code-vs-prose mistake and as touching a previously-hardened security module (REQ-018's eventStaffAuthorization.ts) -- both given extra scrutiny.

1. ZERO IMPLEMENTATION CODE CHECK (exhaustive, all 11 fenced blocks enumerated): lines 64-68 (StartPayload union addition -- bare type), 130-151 (QrCheckinLookup interface + getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin signature -- bare, ends `;`), 183-189 (getCheckinActorDisplayName signature -- bare), 239-255 (QrCheckinDecisionInput/QrCheckinOutcome types + decideQrCheckinOutcome signature -- bare; the 4-row decision rule is stated as a first-match-wins TABLE at line 260-265, never as an if/else body), 288-296 (performQrCheckIn signature -- bare; its 7-step sequence, lines 298-336, is numbered prose describing SQL/writes, not a function body), 350-364 (OverrideDecisionInput/OverrideOutcome types + decideOverrideOutcome signature -- bare; 3-row table at 368-372), 392-399 (overrideAdmitAndCheckIn signature -- bare), 476-492 (buildCheckinRefusalAudit/requireEventStaffForEvent extended signatures -- bare, ends `;`; the entity/entityId mapping is a 2-row TABLE at 496-498, not a branch written as code), 516-524 (resolveCheckinQrDeepLink signature -- bare), 567-572 (CHECKIN_OVERRIDE_PATTERN regex constant + makeCheckinOverrideCallbackHandler with an ellipsis `{ ... }` body -- precedent for both already established and PASSED at REQ-026 (REMINDER24H_*_PATTERN) and REQ-028 (CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN/CHECKIN_PAGE_PATTERN, cross-checked against handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-01b-design-validator.json item 1), 606-628 (checkinQr i18n catalog -- bare type). Grepped the whole document's logic-bearing sections for `if (`, `return <expr>;` (non-outcome-literal), arithmetic, `for`/`while` -- none found outside the accounted-for stub lines. VERDICT: clean, no implementation code.

2. EVENTSTAFFAUTHORIZATION.TS BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY -- VERIFIED BY DIRECT READ of the actual current file (apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts, not the design's citation): buildCheckinRefusalAudit today (lines 102-122) takes exactly 3 params (user, eventId, reason) and always returns entity:'event'/entityId:eventId; requireEventStaffForEvent today (lines 130-147) takes exactly 5 params (db, tgId, eventId, eventEndsAt, evaluationTime) and calls buildCheckinRefusalAudit with exactly those same 3 args. Grepped every call site in apps/bot/src: handlers/checkin.ts lines 206, 248, 339 (REQ-018's /checkin list command, REQ-028's toggle and page-turn callbacks) -- all three pass exactly 5 positional arguments, none pass a 6th. The design's proposed change adds exactly one new OPTIONAL parameter (registrationId?: string) at the END of each function's existing parameter list. In TypeScript this is unconditionally backward-compatible for every existing call: an omitted trailing optional parameter binds to `undefined` at the call site with no source change required, and the design's own table (lines 496-498) states undefined -> unchanged entity:'event'/entityId:eventId behavior. I traced this is not just a claim but structurally guaranteed: no existing call site can accidentally start passing a 6th argument, and no code path threads a stray value into the new parameter's slot by side effect (the only caller of the new parameter, resolveCheckinQrDeepLink section 6.1 step 4, is itself new code in this same design). CONFIRMED backward-compatible, not merely asserted.

3. AC1 REFUSAL-AUDIT REQUIREMENT -- verified distinct from REQ-018's existing event-level refusal audit. REQ-018/028's existing refusal audit (unchanged for every existing caller) always names entity:'event'/entityId:eventId, which cannot satisfy AC1's 'names ... the registration' wording since no registration is in play at those call sites (checkin.ts never has a specific registration at authorization time). The design's extension is the only code path in the codebase that supplies a registrationId to this gate (resolveCheckinQrDeepLink, section 6.1 step 4, is the design's own new call site) -- confirmed this produces entity:'registration'/entityId:registrationId per the table, genuinely satisfying 'actor, action, and the registration' distinctly from the pre-existing event-level row, which continues to serve REQ-018/028's own unrelated call sites unchanged.

4. S4 STALE-TOKEN RECHECK -- traced the exact scenario against the actual current registration.ts, not assumed. Read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts lines 150-255 (registerForEvent) directly: when an existing registration row was withdrawn (existingRegistrationId !== null, line 162) and the same user re-registers, the SAME registration id is UPDATEd (lines 204-214) with a freshly generated qrToken (line 196, 210) if the new outcome is 'admitted'. This is a real, reachable, already-shipped code path (REQ-020/022) -- not hypothetical. A registration id can therefore carry an old, now-superseded qr_token if an attendee withdrew and re-registered between an old QR code being printed/screenshotted and a rescan. (The waitlist-promotion path, generateQrToken called again around line 424-428, is a second, independent instance of the same pattern -- same registration id, freshly issued token.) JUDGMENT: the S4 recheck is correctly scoped, not over-engineering -- it closes a gap in a currently-reachable scenario, using data (`qr_token`) already fetched by the same locked SELECT the transaction needs anyway for the row-lock (§3.3 step 1), at zero extra query cost. This is defensive-but-warranted design, not speculative hardening against an unreachable case.

5. S7 CAPACITY-BYPASS REASONING -- checked against S7's actual text in security-invariants.md (not the design's paraphrase): S7 states verbatim '`seats_taken` exceeds `capacity` only via an explicit organizer override that writes an `AuditLog` row (PRD §12.2)' -- this literally names organizer override as THE named exception, confirming the design's citation (section 4.1) is accurate, not an invented reading. decideOverrideOutcome correctly omits any capacity/seatsLeft check and the design states why (re-running it would contradict the exact invariant this transition exists to satisfy) -- consistent with S7's text.

6. AC2 'REPORT WITHOUT WRITING' -- verified performQrCheckIn's already-checked-in branch (section 3.3 step 5) performs literally zero writes: the design states 'no write' explicitly, distinguishing 'already-checked-in' from 'check-in' as separate outcome-table entries precisely so the write (step 6, only reached for 'check-in') is never executed on a repeat scan. The report uses the freshly locked row's own checked_in_by/checked_in_at (read in the same FOR UPDATE SELECT, step 1) -- not the earlier unlocked §2.1 snapshot -- via getCheckinActorDisplayName (§2.2), called by the handler (§6.1 step 9) using outcome's own checked_in_by. This correctly returns the ORIGINAL, unmodified values rather than anything the current scan attempt might otherwise introduce. No no-op UPDATE is present anywhere in the sequence.

7. ALL 7 ACs MAPPED (§10 table) -- each row names concrete section(s)/mechanism(s): AC1 (§5 extension + §6.1 steps 4-5), AC2 (§3.2 outcome distinction + §3.3 step 5 + §2.2 + §6.1 steps 9-10), AC3 (§3.2 per-admission table + §3.3 step 4 + §6.1 step 8), AC4 (§2.1 null return + §3.3 step 2 token-currency + requireEventStaffForEvent's existing event-ended branch), AC5 (§2.1's structural phone/email exclusion + §6.1 step 10), AC6 (§4.2's single UPDATE + single writeAuditLog + §4.3's authorization gate), AC7 (§1's single new entry point + §8's explicit absence-of-WebApp confirmation, cross-checked against a stated `git grep` invariant). No TBD/deferral language found; all 4 open questions (§9) each name a real residual gap with reasoned accept/defer, not placeholders for undone design work -- consistent with the precedent already accepted at REQ-028's gate.

8. TOKENS/DESIGN-SYSTEM CHECK -- §12 states no design-system token/component applies (bot has no visual/CSS surface); confirmed no color/spacing/typography reference appears anywhere in the document to check against docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/tokens.css. Correct N/A, matching REQ-016/017/018/028's identical, previously-accepted reasoning for this bot surface.

9. SCHEMA CLAIM (§0) -- design states no schema change; independently spot-checked qr_token/checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method and the unique index/CHECK constraint are pre-existing per REQ-028's own already-verified schema read (handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-01b-design-validator.json item 2) -- no new claim introduced here beyond what that prior, independently-verified read already confirmed for the same columns/constraints.

Verdict: PASS. Zero implementation code found. The eventStaffAuthorization.ts extension is genuinely, structurally backward-compatible (verified against the actual current file and all 3 real call sites, not asserted). AC1's audit distinctness is real. The S4 stale-token recheck addresses a demonstrably reachable current-code scenario (registerForEvent's withdraw-then-re-register path and the waitlist-promotion path both regenerate qr_token on an existing registration id) and is appropriately, not excessively, scoped. S7's capacity-override exception is accurately cited. AC2's no-write guarantee on repeat scan is genuine. All 7 ACs map to concrete design elements.

context.verification_notes: eventStaffAuthorization.ts's current buildCheckinRefusalAudit/requireEventStaffForEvent signatures (3 and 5 params respectively) independently re-read from apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts lines 102-147; all 3 existing call sites (handlers/checkin.ts lines 206, 248, 339) independently grepped and confirmed to pass exactly the current parameter count, none anticipating a 6th argument. S4 stale-token scenario independently traced against apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts lines 150-255 (registerForEvent's withdraw-then-re-register UPDATE path, line 196/210) and the waitlist-promotion path (~line 424-428), both confirmed to regenerate qr_token on an existing registration id in already-shipped code. security-invariants.md S7's exact text confirmed to name organizer override as the capacity-bypass exception verbatim.
